title: Weighted sum after a coordinate flip
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $V$ be a real normed vector space, let $w_0,\ldots,w_{n-1}\in V$, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, and choose a coordinate $i$. The weighted sum of the signs after flipping coordinate $i$ equals the original weighted sum minus twice the contribution from coordinate $i$; that is, $\sum_j x'_j w_j=\sum_j x_jw_j-2x_iw_i$, where $x'$ agrees with $x$ except that $x'_i=-x_i$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a real normed vector space
$w$ assigns a vector in $V$ to each coordinate
$x$ is a sign vector of length $n$
